dimensions.assessment: Involves federal agency leadership, border personnel, and congressional committees receiving the assessments.
dimensions.evidence: Secretary of Homeland Security, in coordination with the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection and the Administrator of General Services

dimensions.assessment: Primarily administrative, mandating reports and briefings on existing standards, staffing, and delays.
dimensions.evidence: submit to the Committee on Homeland Security of the House... an assessment of the current standards and guidelines

dimensions.assessment: Does not state or imply any appropriations, grants, or direct fiscal changes.
Establishes a new recurring reporting mandate for DHS and related agencies.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act and annually thereafter

dimensions.assessment: Requires ongoing annual assessments and subsequent briefings indefinitely.

importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires recurring assessments and congressional briefings regarding staffing levels, delays, and operations at air, land, and sea ports of entry under the Department of Homeland Security, without altering spending or agency powers directly.
